import pandas as pd

# Read source table with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_89/training_0.csv", index_col=0)

# UNPIVOT operation: melt all columns except 'date' into key-value pairs
unpivoted = source.melt(id_vars=['date'], value_vars=['ticker', 'open', 'high', 'low', 'close', 'volume', 'adj_close', 'adj_volume'],
                        var_name='ticker', value_name='value')

# PIVOT operation: pivot the unpivoted data to have 'date' as index and unique 'ticker' values as columns
pivoted = unpivoted.pivot(index='date', columns='ticker', values='value')

# Reset index to bring 'date' back as a column
pivoted = pivoted.reset_index()

# The target schema has 'date' as string and many float columns named by float values (which correspond to ticker values)
# The pivoted columns are ticker values as strings, so convert column names to float to match target schema
pivoted.columns = ['date'] + [float(str(col)) for col in pivoted.columns[1:]]

# Sort columns to match the target schema order (date first, then sorted float columns)
pivoted = pivoted[['date'] + sorted(pivoted.columns[1:])]

# Write the final output to the target file path
pivoted.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length1_89/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
